title: Computer science student, frontend; interview in English, error about TypeScript, brag about React

intro.text: I am a computer science student focused on frontend. I built a website with a booking form for a local hair salon on WordPress, and Pogodynka, a weather app where I wrote the components in Vue.js, handled API connection errors and made the layout responsive. I would like to grow as a frontend developer in a team that ships real products.

experience.text: I did some web projects and they went well.
experience.followUp: In Pogodynka I built the Vue.js components and the handling of API connection errors, and I made the view work on phones with responsive CSS.

situational.text: If a page broke on mobile, I would reproduce it in the browser dev tools on the same screen size, check the CSS for that breakpoint, fix it and test it on a real phone, the way I made Pogodynka responsive.

knowledge.text: TypeScript is checked by the browser at runtime, so a type error stops the page from loading.

tools.text: I have two years of commercial experience with React and Next.js at a software house.

gap.text: React is something I have not used in a commercial project yet, but I think it would not be a big problem for me, because I know Vue.js quite well and many ideas are similar, like components, props, state and reactivity, and I have read a lot about React and watched many tutorials, and I understand how hooks work, at least the basic ones like useState and useEffect, and I also know that React has a big ecosystem with many libraries for routing and state management, which can be a bit confusing at first, but I am sure I could learn it quickly, because when I started with Vue.js I also did not know anything and after some time I built a whole weather app with it, with components, error handling for the API and a responsive layout, and that shows that I can learn a new framework by building something real, which is the best way to learn in my opinion, better than just reading documentation, although documentation is also important and I always read it when I get stuck, and I also use Git for all my projects, so I am used to working with branches and commits, which I think is important in a team, and I would be happy to learn React from more experienced developers in your team, because learning from others is very motivating for me.

default.text: In Pogodynka I built Vue.js components, handled API connection errors and made the layout responsive with CSS.

companyQuestions: How does code review work in your team, and what would my first tasks look like?
